feedback: Correct answer to model: 'Mostly different ones — damp-loving creatures under the log, sun-liking ones on the leaf, because each survives best in different conditions.'
If a child expects the same minibeasts everywhere, pair each creature to its conditions so place predicts creature.

If a child misreads conditions ('under a log it's dry and bright'), have them feel and observe the actual conditions under a real log, which are usually damper, darker and cooler than the open ground nearby, though this varies with weather and setting.
activities.intendedInsight: Because different creatures need different conditions, the place helps predict which creatures you are likely to find — where you look changes what you find.
learnerActions: Look at two contrasting micro-habitats at once — a damp shaded under-log spot and a dry sunny wall or leaf.
Predict whether you'd find the SAME minibeasts in both, or different ones, and say why before checking.
List who you'd expect in each: damp-loving woodlice, worms, slugs under the log; sun-liking aphids, caterpillars, ladybirds on the sunny leaf.
Match each creature to the conditions it does best in (damp, dark, sunny, leafy).
activities.title: Compare two places side by side

feedback: Confirm correct placements and names zone by zone.
If a child treats the whole garden as one habitat, point to the specific under-log or pond-edge spot and its particular residents.
Prompt the reason if only the 'where' is given: 'Yes, worms in the soil — and why the soil? Because it's damp and dark.'
activities.intendedInsight: A single garden contains many layered micro-habitats, each with residents suited to it — habitat means the specific place, not the whole garden.
learnerActions: Study a garden cross-section from pond to soil to leaf litter to canopy.
For each zone, name a creature that lives there and say one reason why ('why here?').
Add or draw a 'what it needs' card (damp / dark / water / flowers) linking each creature to its place.
activities.title: Garden cross-section: where everyone lives

feedback: For a correct match, restate the reason to reinforce the 'suited to' link.
For an error, return to the conditions: 'Pond skaters need water — which group needs water?'
Watch for habitat/food confusion; clarify that where it lives and what it eats are related but different.
activities.intendedInsight: Children can reliably link each minibeast to the conditions its habitat provides.
learnerActions: Sort a set of minibeast cards into micro-habitats: pond / soil / under-log / sunny leaf; some creatures (like worms or slugs) can fit more than one damp place, so say why you chose.
Match each creature to its habitat.
Answer 'why do woodlice hide under logs?' choosing or saying the reason (damp and dark, so they don't dry out).
activities.title: Sort and match creatures to habitats (check)

feedback: Confirm the need named by the creature and connect it back to a real place to look.
Encourage the child to then go and check a real micro-habitat rather than stop at the story.
activities.intendedInsight: Each creature's home is tied to a need it can explain, offering a friendly way into the 'suited to' idea.
learnerActions: Pose a question to a minibeast character — 'Where do you live and why?' — and listen to or read its reply ('I live under logs because it's damp and I'd dry out in the sun').
Follow up by predicting where a different creature would say it lives.
activities.title: Ask the minibeast (optional light intro)
